# sound_rs

> Fast Rust audio for Python: play, stream and record WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG and M4A
> without ffmpeg, with bounded playback streaming and a typed API. Python 3.10+, wheels for Linux
> x86_64/aarch64, Windows amd64, macOS arm64/Intel.

Version 0.4.0. Install with `pip install sound_rs`. Playback waits release
the GIL; decoding returns float32 `(frames, channels)` arrays; library failures raise
`sound_rs.SoundRsError` with a `.code` of `io`, `format`, `device`, `stalled`,
`unsupported` or `usage`.
Python argument conversion can raise TypeError or OverflowError. Linux wheels require
the ALSA runtime. Full load/load_many and recording retain samples in memory.
Create, use and destroy each Player/Recorder on the same thread. Playback waits release
the GIL; preparation and teardown can still hold it. record_to captures in memory, then writes.

Reading order for a coding task: Overview, Quickstart, then the guide for the job
(player, datasets, recording, writing, numpy, migration), then the API reference.
Skipping the guides and guessing the API is the most common way to get it wrong.

## Start

- [Overview](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/index.html.md): sound_rs plays, records and decodes audio in Python, with built-in decoders, bounded playback streaming, NumPy arrays and WAV output.
- [Installation](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/install.html.md): How to install sound_rs: wheels for Linux, Windows and macOS, Python versions, from-source builds, and the Linux audio library it needs.
- [Quickstart](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/quickstart.html.md): The five things most sound_rs code does: play a file, control it, play an array, read metadata, decode to NumPy.
- [Command line](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/cli.html.md): The soundrs command: play a file, inspect metadata, list output devices, and find the documentation from a terminal.

## Guides

- [The player](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/player.html.md): The sound_rs Player: one stream kept open, playback, pause, resume, stop, seeking, thread ownership and source lifecycle.
- [Streaming and memory](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/streaming.html.md): How bounded playback buffers differ from whole-file decoding, what historical memory measurements show, and when to use load().
- [Formats and gapless](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/formats.html.md): Which formats and bit depths sound_rs decodes, how encoder delay and padding are trimmed, and what the MP3 offset against libsndfile means.
- [NumPy and arrays](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/numpy.html.md): Array shapes, dtype rules, playing and decoding arrays with sound_rs, batch decoding, and the mistakes that cost the most time.
- [Datasets and ML](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/datasets.html.md): Load audio for machine learning: one call to resample to 16 kHz mono, parallel decoding across cores, and honest memory numbers.
- [Recording](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/recording.html.md): Record from a microphone with sound_rs: input devices, start/stop, fixed-length captures, macOS permissions, and writing a WAV.
- [Writing WAV files](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/writing.html.md): Write frames-first float32 arrays as PCM16, PCM24 or float32 WAV; understand clipping, validation, errors and memory limits.
- [Coming from another library](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/migration.html.md): Equivalent sound_rs code for sounddevice, soundfile, pydub and playsound, plus what changes when there is no ffmpeg and no array requirement.

## Reference

- [API reference](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/api.html.md): Every function and method in sound_rs: signatures, arguments, return values, exceptions and a runnable example.
- [Benchmarks](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/benchmarks.html.md): How sound_rs compares with libsndfile and sounddevice: methodology, full tables, and the cases where it loses.
- [Guarantees](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/guarantees.html.md): sound_rs error contracts, thread ownership, regression checks, memory limits and the boundaries of device and security validation.
- [Troubleshooting](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/faq.html.md): Common sound_rs problems: no sound, busy device, ALSA and PipeWire on Linux, Jupyter, asyncio, and why the first play is slower.
- [Changelog](https://neksand.github.io/sound_rs/changelog.html.md): sound_rs release history: what changed in each version and where to find the full release notes.

  where sound_rs loses
